title: Basel Framework — CAP (Definition of capital)
sourceNote: Structured rendering of the BCBS consolidated Basel Framework, standard group CAP (Definition of capital), in force from 2019-12-15. This is the bank's working representation for horizon-scan extraction; the verbatim source is the BIS consolidated framework at https://www.bis.org/basel_framework/standard/CAP.htm. Binds the bank via SARB transposition (Regulations Relating to Banks Reg 38).

sections.heading: Minimum risk-based capital requirements
sections.text: A bank must maintain regulatory capital, measured against its total risk-weighted assets (RWA), at no less than the minimum ratios set out below at all times. Regulatory capital comprises three components in descending order of loss-absorbing quality: Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1), Additional Tier 1 (AT1), and Tier 2 (T2).

subsections.text: Common Equity Tier 1 capital must be at least 4.5% of risk-weighted assets at all times. CET1 is the highest-quality, fully loss-absorbing capital: common shares issued by the bank that meet the criteria for classification as common shares, the associated stock surplus, retained earnings, and accumulated other comprehensive income, net of regulatory adjustments.
Tier 1 capital, being the sum of Common Equity Tier 1 and Additional Tier 1 capital, must be at least 6.0% of risk-weighted assets at all times.
Total capital, being the sum of Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital, must be at least 8.0% of risk-weighted assets at all times.

sections.heading: Capital buffers above the regulatory minimum
sections.text: Buffers sit above the Pillar 1 minima and constrain capital distributions when they are not met, rather than triggering breach of the minimum requirement.

subsections.text: A bank must hold a capital conservation buffer of 2.5% of risk-weighted assets, composed of Common Equity Tier 1 capital, above the 4.5% CET1 minimum. A bank whose CET1 falls within the buffer range becomes subject to constraints on the distribution of earnings (dividends, share buy-backs and discretionary staff bonuses) calibrated to how far into the buffer it has fallen.
